--- PART 1/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "We need improve parent slot 6." / "Parent is essentially biased TFT with nice and retaliation, forgiving moderate. Fitness ~276.12, close to best slot 11 280.1."
STRATEGY: Parent slot 6 is described as a biased TFT with retaliation and moderate forgiveness; the trace simulates the 12 population slots and archive, then plans a more adaptive TFT-like strategy with probing, forgiveness, and endgame defection.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the complexity, maybe the simplest high-scoring strategy is 'Tit-for-Tat with forgiveness, plus defect on the last round if opponent cooperated last round'."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy (slot 11-like) that cooperates by default and retaliates to defection. The trace simulates the 12 population slots against probing/defection and endgame defection, and proposes changes: always defect on the last round, defect on round 99 if the opponent seems forgiving, and possibly add occasional probing.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So a simple rule: always defect on rounds 99 and 100 (i.e., n>=98)." and "Let's design this strategy concretely."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that cooperates until the endgame and defects on the last round(s). The trace simulates it against slots 0–11, computes payoffs, and revises it by adding an early probe at round 20 to classify opponents as forgiving or retaliating, then exploiting forgiving opponents by defecting the last 14 rounds while only defecting the final round against retaliators.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So a strategy: if is_forgiving, from round 75 onwards, defect on odd rounds? But we need to know the round number. We can just use n."
STRATEGY: Parent is a complex TFT with forgiveness thresholds; trace simulates a probe at round 20 and endgame exploitation against forgiving opponents; changed to add a probe, alternating endgame defections, and a last-round defect.
